To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the novel device n-MISSIFET with dielectric stack is a promising candidate for future nanoscale applications.
the n-MISISFETS are suitable for nano-scale devices.
the proposed device n-MISISFIT has a better performance in terms of threshold voltage and transconductance as compared to n-MOSFTE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of n-MISIS-FET in nano-regimes, the simulation of the device and the analysis of the results.
the study of the behaviour of n-MISIS-FET in nano regime.
a new n-MISISFTE with a `dielectic stack' instead of a single insulator in n-MOSFTE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the n-MISISFETS can be a potential alternative to n-MOSFETS for future VLSI circuits.
the n-MISISFETS are more promising for low voltage and low power applications.
, the n-MISISFETS are the best candidate for future generation nano-electronics devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the novel n-MISSFET has been proposed, designed and simulated using TCAD.
the novel n-MISFET with a dielectric stack is an attractive alternative to the conventional n-MOSFETS in nano regime.
the n-MISISFETS with `dielectric stack', as compared to the conventional MOSFETs, can have the advantage of higher current gain and lower threshold voltage, which can be controlled by the body bias.
The main takeaway from our work is that
n-MISISFETS can be used in the nano regime for the first time.
the n-MISISFETS with `dielectric stack', instead of the single dielectric, can be used as an alternative to the n-MOSFETS for low voltage applications and also for low power applications.
, the threshold voltage of the n-MISISFTE can be controlled by forward and reverse body biases.
